visual_text: Risk factors from two heatwave studies
1. Top floor under the roof: higher risk
3. Does not leave home each day, or confined to bed: higher risk
5. Friends nearby and a way to get out: lower risk (Chicago)
6. Light clothing and ways to cool down: lower risk (France)
Check daily on older neighbours who live alone. This is a judgement drawn from studies of who died; they show links, not proof of cause.
Semenza et al., NEJM, 1996 (Chicago 1995); Vandentorren et al., Eur J Public Health, 2006 (France 2003)
alt_text: Drawing of a room with an older woman in a light top sitting in an armchair by a window, and a man standing at the left holding a glass. Six numbered keys: top floor, living alone, not leaving home or confined to bed raised heatwave risk; air conditioning, friends and a way out, light clothing lowered it. Links, not proof.
